limitations: Review covers only the supplied excerpts. I did not see the full factory-receipt-archive.py, state.canonical, state.require, process.run or no_duplicate_keys, so I assumed require raises ValueError and canonical is deterministic.
I did not execute the test script. I traced it by hand against the source: call counts, route rejections, duplicate-key JSON, and the cache byte-bound message.

The claim that _origin_ancestor is the only consumer of this selector comes from your factory-wide search. I could not re-verify it here, and a consumer that read signature or user annotations from a cached compare response would see stale data.

I assumed GitHub compare with per_page=1&page=2 returns small, paginated responses. If files are not paginated, large diffs could hit the cache or budget byte limits sooner. That fails closed, and the cache does not make it worse than the uncached path.
I do not infer native or cadence behavior, a full 1001-invocation PASS, or the final-tail actual acceptance result. Those stay separate.
I did not check whether the new test script is wired into any CI or test runner.
structured_output.review_summary: No actionable defects found. The predicate in _once runs after _route, so the foreign-repo, method, raw, encoded-path and '..' checks all apply first. The cache key is the exact path string. The regex is fullmatch with repo-escaped root, 40-hex SHAs and the literal query ?per_page=1&page=2, so any other query, order, page, ref or branch form either misses the cache or is rejected by _route. Ancestry between two commit SHAs is a property of immutable commit objects, so it stays valid after ref or policy changes. Mutable ref, repo, ruleset and rules reads remain uncached and fresh. A failed gh call raises before anything is cached. A response with duplicate keys or invalid JSON raises before caching. Serialization goes through encode(), which applies the existing node, string and byte bounds, and the _immutable_bytes <= MAX_BYTES check raises on overflow instead of caching past the limit. Hits return a fresh json.loads of the stored canonical bytes, so callers cannot mutate the cache. Hits skip budget.begin/observe, so only physical fetches are charged, which matches the intended dedup of the 223 duplicate comparisons. _origin_ancestor reads only base_commit.sha, merge_base_commit.sha, status, behind_by, ahead_by and total_commits, all immutable for a SHA pair, so the cache does not affect its security predicate. The tests cover single physical fetch, deepcopy isolation, raw-byte accounting, sibling-selector misses, mutable freshness, route rejections without a fetch, duplicate-key JSON not cached, and the cache byte cap.
